correctness.rationale: On X,Y>0, principal square roots u=√X, v=√Y obey u′=(v−1)/2 and v′=(r−u)/2; therefore (u−r,v−1) is a circle with angular speed −1/2. The forbidden u≤0 and v≤0 closed phase intervals have half widths α and β and centers a quarter turn apart. The number of connected positive arcs changes at m=min(r,1), M=max(r,1) and at their overlap radius R=√(r²+1). A complete period exists only below m; one positive arc for m≤ρ<M, two for M≤ρ<R and one for ρ≥R. Multiplying angular lengths by 2 derives the stated durations, while differentiating α+β at R gives short-flight decay 2R(R−ρ)/r+O((R−ρ)^2). At X=0, the axis path and a delayed outgoing square-root harmonic arc share the same C1 derivative, establishing nonunique local nonnegative continuation. For r=1 the middle one-arc regime is empty. Numeric phase sampling cannot replace this exact proof.
